objective: Proof and computation. On a knot's space, count the colourings of each side of every nontrivial 2- and 3-edge cut with its channel values fixed: the count is the same for every accepted assignment (complement symmetry; the point lemma and the one-amplitude theorem), and the two sides' counts multiply to the amplitude of the whole. So counted length, the logarithm of a part's count, is additive over the decomposition into parts: a measure, worth log 5 per Fano atom plus the logarithm of the glue's tree-trinity number. Along a route of m Fano units it is m log 5, which relations (length mod 2) cannot see; in rings of units cut from different spaces the relation and the count vary independently. It is unchanged by transposition and by isomorphism, but not by replacing a part with a relationally equal one. Read against the program: a law-intrinsic measure on substrate routes, not a native extended distance.
status: Proved by SELECT-COUNT-20261101-001B-P001: across every nontrivial 2- or 3-edge cut of a knot's space each side has one count on its accepted channel values and the two counts multiply to the amplitude (the twist identity with complement symmetry and one amplitude), so counted length is additive over the decomposition: log 5 per Fano block plus the glue's tree-trinity logarithm (twisted cube 6 log 5 + log 2), m log 5 along m units where relations keep m mod 2; in rings of units cut from different spaces the relation (parity of the number of units) and the count (product of amplitudes) vary independently; unchanged by transposition and isomorphism, not by relationally equal replacement; a law-intrinsic measure on substrate routes, not a native extended distance
title: Counted length is a measure on the knot's spaces
